content:
We've heard plenty of rumors about Apple's next-generation iPad mini, including an OLED display and improved water resistance.

A new leak today claims the upcoming iPad mini will feature a powerful new A20 Pro processor.

MacRumors discovered references to the next-generation iPad mini in Apple's system code today, including what appears to be a product icon for the device.

The icon shows the new iPad mini will look largely the same as the current model, but the camera has been moved from the top bezel to the landscape side, aligning it with Apple's other iPad models. There's also a small speaker cutout at the top of the display, similar to the iPhone design.

The code also mentions the new iPad mini will be powered by the A20 Pro processor, the same chip used in the iPhone 18 Pro lineup launched last week. The current iPad mini, released in October 2024, uses an Apple A17 Pro processor.

According to Mark Gurman, the new iPad mini is expected to launch by the end of October. In addition to the changes mentioned above, the new iPad mini is also rumored to feature improved water resistance and a redesigned speaker system.

For more details, check out our full preview of the new iPad mini.

A separate report has also revealed specifications for the next-generation base iPad, including an A19 processor, 8GB of RAM, and Apple's own N1 and C1X connectivity chips.
